sources.claim: Deng et al. (NAACL 2024), "Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models": test items can leak into training data, which can inflate benchmark scores; simple overlap checks can miss contaminated examples.

sections.skill: Explain what a benchmark score shows and its limits

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: What is a benchmark?

choices.text: A standard test used to compare models
A company's ranking of its own staff
A long bench in a computer lab

questions.correct_answer: A standard test used to compare models
questions.intro: A BENCHMARK is a standard test used to compare models, such as a set of math problems or reading questions with known answers. A high score shows the model did well on THAT test. It may not predict how well the model does YOUR task, which may use different topics, formats or languages. Benchmarks can also be affected by CONTAMINATION: test questions that leaked into the model's training data, so the model may have seen the answers. Researchers (Deng and others, 2024) found contamination can inflate scores and is hard to detect. Use benchmarks as a rough guide, then test on your own examples.

sections.skill: Compare a benchmark with a driving test

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: What does passing a driving test show?

choices.text: You can do the tested skills on that day
That you can drive perfectly in every condition anywhere in the world for the rest of your life

questions.correct_answer: You can do the tested skills on that day
questions.intro: A DRIVING TEST checks set skills on a set route: parking, signaling, a few turns. Passing shows you can do those things on that day. It does not prove you can drive in a snowstorm or on a mountain road. And if someone memorized the exact route and every turn in advance, a pass would show even less. A benchmark is like a driving test: useful, but limited to what it tests, and less meaningful if the answers were known beforehand.

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: All top models score about 99 on a benchmark. What does this mean?

choices.text: It no longer separates them well
That every model is now perfect

questions.correct_answer: It no longer separates them well
questions.intro: Scores invite over-reading. A difference of one or two points may be noise. A benchmark can become "saturated" when top models all score near 100, so it no longer separates them. Marketing may quote only the benchmarks a model does well on. Ask: What exactly does the test measure? Is it like my task? Who ran it, and how? Then check with a small test set of your own.
